focus.jbig: Chip rout hits from Asia · earnings strong, but Fed lands tomorrow
focus.jtag: Semis sell off globally on AI-financing fears; KO/DINO beat, oil eases; FOMC decision Wed 7/29
focus.jnote: Split tape — a chip-led risk-off in tech against earnings-driven strength elsewhere. US tech slid before the bell as a sell-off in Korean memory makers underscored AI circular-financing worries — South Korea's Kospi tumbled over 10%, with SK Hynix and Samsung sinking more than 14% and 13%. Nasdaq 100 futures fell nearly 1% while S&P futures were roughly flat and Dow futures rose ~0.6% on strong quarterly results. Reports that Nvidia is exploring a large funding backstop for OpenAI further intertwined the two names and soured AI sentiment. Oil eased toward $82–83 on the U.S.–Iran pause. But the Fed's two-day meeting concludes tomorrow (Wed 7/29) with a decision expected to hold — a scheduled rate event inside the window caps today at YELLOW.
focus.notdown: Today's boarded bulls are the cleanest longs: FBP (a held ATH breakout in a Puerto-Rico bank) and the earnings gappers KO and DINO — their catalysts are behind them and levels are freshly minted. But an FOMC surprise tomorrow can reprice rate-sensitive names in seconds, so any bull put must be 7-DTE, expire before the decision, and go on at half size.
focus.notup: Chips / AI-heavy tech (NVDA, MU, AMD, SanDisk) are under heavy pressure on AI-spend and circular-financing fears. That's a fundamental lean lower, but selling bear calls into an FOMC-week VIX — where one dovish line can rip a short-squeeze — is not a probability edge. Stand aside on new bearish premium until the Fed clears.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? The FOMC decision is inside the next 24h — the master rule says a scheduled Fed event in the window cannot be GREEN and defaults to YELLOW (A-grade only, half size, 7-DTE that clears the event). Composite ~54 is in WARM and P(≥1% gap) ~34% is right on the 35% line. Markets lean to a hold but still price meaningful hike odds later in the year on the energy-driven inflation. The de-escalation in oil is good news, so this isn't RED — but disciplined sizing and short DTE are non-negotiable.
